title: A stale-timestamp webhook is refused; a replayed delivery id is acknowledged once and never delivered twice
asA: operator whose project stores state keyed on delivery events
iWant: the verifier to reject replays inside the tolerance window and acknowledge duplicates without re-invoking the handler
soThat: a captured signed request cannot corrupt downstream state and the provider's retry-on-non-2xx behaviour stays idempotent-safe

acceptanceCriteria.description: A webhook POST whose timestamp header is older than the configured tolerance window is refused with HTTP 401 and an empty body; the downstream handler is not invoked and a `webhookReplayStale` audit event is emitted.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running project with a configured tolerance window of 300 seconds and a POST whose timestamp header is set to a value 301 or more seconds in the past
acceptanceCriteria.when: the POST is delivered to the webhook route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 401, the response body is empty, the handler invocation counter is unchanged, and the audit sink observes exactly one `webhookReplayStale` event

acceptanceCriteria.description: A signature-valid webhook POST whose delivery event id already appears in the bounded event-id store is acknowledged with HTTP 200 without invoking the downstream handler; a `webhookReplayDuplicate` audit event is emitted.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running project with a signature-valid POST that has already been processed once (event id recorded in the store) and a second POST carrying the same event id inside the tolerance window
acceptanceCriteria.when: the second POST is delivered to the webhook route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 200, the handler invocation counter is unchanged from before the second POST, and the audit sink observes exactly one `webhookReplayDuplicate` event on the second POST
